blocks.text: # Fixed Workflow and Treatment Boundary
## Why this is genuinely a handoff study

An ordinary Harvey LAB task can be solved by one agent. That is useful as a real legal-work substrate, but it does not itself test lineage. Our wrapper makes the handoff real by requiring separate fresh-session agents to produce and consume intermediate work products. The handoff is not gratuitous: evidence extraction, decision acceptance, drafting, and final acceptance are distinct legal-work functions whose artifacts are routinely reviewed or revised by different people/agents.
## Fixed centralized multi-agent system

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant H as Harvey harness
    participant OP as Orchestrator (planning session)
    participant E as Evidence agent
    participant D as Decision agent
    participant W as Drafting agent
    participant OR as Orchestrator (review session; same role)
    H->>OP: Task workspace + role-independent task instruction
    OP->>E: materialize V0 handoff; fresh receiver
    E->>D: materialize V1 handoff; fresh receiver
    D->>W: materialize V2 handoff; fresh receiver
    W->>OR: materialize V3 handoff; fresh receiver
    OR->>OR: V4 accept, request revision, or abstain
    OR-->>H: Final deliverable + run manifest
    H->>H: Official rubric + provenance checks
```

There is one orchestrator **role**, shown as `OP` and `OR` only because planning and review are separate fresh sessions. The handoff materializer is deterministic harness code, not an extra agent. Specialists do not message one another outside materialized inputs. If a later frozen matrix enables revision, the request and returned artifact become declared checkpoints; no role carries private memory between stages.
## What stays constant

| Controlled factor | Rule |
|---|---|
| Task | same pinned Harvey task ID, source files, hashes, deliverable, scorer |
| Architecture | same orchestrator role, specialist roles, stage order, revision cap, and fresh-session rule |
| Tools | same official Harvey tool policy and sandbox |
| Model | same exact homogeneous-team configuration within a paired comparison |
| Budget | same stage time/tool/output caps; handoff-visible tokens matched within 5% |
| Isolated diagnostic | all representations derive from one frozen canonical checkpoint history |
| End-to-end workflow | all arms start from the same task, but later artifacts may diverge as the treatment accumulates |
| Judge | official Harvey rubric blind to arm; provenance audit blind to arm/model labels |
## Accepted follow-up: what varies

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  T["Pinned Harvey task"] --> S["single-agent\nunified session"]
  T --> M["centralized shared-memory MAS\nmutable coordination.md"]
  T --> P["centralized Proofpress-native MAS\nembedded admitted history in work artifacts"]
  M --> R["Harvey scorer"]
  P --> R
  S --> R
```

The centralized communication baseline is deliberately strong: all five fresh sessions may read and update one ordinary prose `coordination.md` file. It contains decisions, rationale, open questions, and next actions, but not typed source classes, decision/acceptance status, authority, signatures/hashes, capsule identifiers, or verification state. In the Proofpress-native arm that sidecar is absent: the same eligible history is embedded in the actual evidence map, decision register, draft, and final artifact. Proofpress adds no legal facts, better model, source document, or secret evaluator. The primary fair question is therefore “shared mutable coordination memory versus document-native admitted lineage,” not “one sidecar Markdown format versus another.”
## Lineage capsule contract
At each accepted V1–V4 checkpoint, the capsule is embedded in the current artifact and records only the claims touched at that checkpoint. Each claim may carry:
The wrapper must verify each embedded capsule before a receiver receives it. A failed verification is a run-level operational event; it may not be silently repaired into a clean treatment input.
## Isolated handoff diagnostic versus end-to-end workflow

The primary study is end-to-end: it measures the cumulative system effect of each arm across V0–V4. This is realistic, but after the first receiver each arm may create different downstream artifacts. The completed isolated sidecar diagnostic is retained as an operational check only. It is not rerun or used as a replacement baseline until a future native-carrier mechanism test is justified.
## Homogeneous model teams and transport

For one workflow slice, OP, E, D, W, and OR all use the same exact model and `high` effort. This prevents a role-model assignment from masquerading as a handoff effect. The Harvey task and scorer remain fixed; an OpenRouter adapter is only a transport layer. It uses concrete model slugs, no `auto` routing, no version aliases, no fallbacks, pinned provider routing, and logs the resolved provider/model, request settings, tokens, and cost metadata.
## Reversal test

The desired behavior is neither blind obedience to history nor casual overwriting. When a later source changes a factual premise, or an explicit expiry/reversal condition is met, the receiver should identify the prior accepted decision, cite the new evidence, and produce a superseding decision. The scorer distinguishes this correct reversal from a decision regression and from a false block.
